title: Solve Systems of Equations by Graphing in Desmos
description: Graph both complete equations, adjust both axis ranges to find hidden intersections, and use every relevant solution to answer the requested quantity.

questions.stem_html: The system consists of \(y=3x+1\) and \(y=-2x+11\). What is the x-coordinate of the solution?
questions.explanation_html: Graph both equations and read the x-coordinate of their common point \((2,7)\). The horizontal coordinate is 2.
questions.variation: Find the shared point of two lines and report the requested coordinate or sum

questions.stem_html: The system consists of \(y=2x-18\) and \(y=x+13\). What is x + y for its solution?
questions.explanation_html: Graph both full equations. They meet only at \((31,44)\), where the sum is 75.
questions.variation: Expand both axes to locate a distant intersection

questions.stem_html: The pair (u, v) solves \(2u+3v=29\) and \(2u-v=1\). What is the value of \(u-v\)?
questions.explanation_html: Use x in place of u and y in place of v to graph both equations. Their intersection has coordinates \((4,7)\). Restore the original roles to compute u − v = -3.
questions.variation: Graph a system in other variables and restore their roles

questions.stem_html: What is the larger x-coordinate of an intersection of \(y=x^{2}+26\) and \(y=2x+2\)?
questions.explanation_html: Graph both equations and find both intersections. Equating them yields \((x+4)(x-6)=0\), so the x-coordinates are -4 and 6. The larger is 6.
questions.variation: Find both intersections of a line and a parabola

questions.stem_html: A system is given by \(y=\sqrt{x-4}+4\) and \(x-13=0\). What is the y-coordinate of the solution?
questions.explanation_html: The second equation graphs as a vertical line at x = 13. It meets the square-root curve at y = 3 + 4 = 7, which also checks by substitution.
questions.variation: Find the intersection of a vertical line and a nonlinear graph

questions.stem_html: How many solutions does the system \(y=4x-3\) and \(y=4x+9\) have?
questions.explanation_html: The slopes are both 4, but the intercepts are -3 and 9. The graphs are distinct parallel lines and never share a point.
questions.variation: Determine the number of solutions when the graphs are parallel
